question: A 52-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of upper abdominal pain and nausea that occurs about 3 hours after eating and at night. These symptoms improve with eating. After eating, he often has a feeling of fullness and bloating. He has had several episodes of dark stools over the past month. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years and drinks 2 alcoholic beverages daily. He takes no medications. His temperature is 36.4°C (97.5°F), pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Abdominal examination shows epigastric tenderness with no guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are normal. Which of the following treatments is most appropriate to prevent further complications of the disease in this patient?
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including upper abdominal pain, nausea, bloating, feeling of fullness, and dark stools, are suggestive of a peptic ulcer disease with possible complications like bleeding. Given his history of smoking and alcohol consumption, he is at increased risk for peptic ulcer disease. The most appropriate treatment to prevent further complications in this patient would be eradication therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection, which is the main cause of peptic ulcers. Therefore, the correct option is to treat with Amoxicillin, clarithromycin, and omeprazole.
